module_summary: dash_main.c is the dashboard shell: section/tab switching, the never-returning DashRun loop (input, per-section callbacks, throttled remote-command/disc/device polls, deferred saves, rendering), the launch paths (dashLaunchApp and runMiscCommand, both ending in ExecuteMainAction), boot-time launch keys and the auto-launch countdown, SELECT+button quick launch, the START menu and the scene-override stack for nested full-screen tools. dash_png.c decodes PNG files through libpng with a streaming box filter straight into a CT32 thumbnail; it is used by the artwork and theme-texture worker jobs (dash_art.c) and by the image viewer on the UI thread (dash_image.c). dash_ps1_card.c is the PS1 card image tool: lists saves, imports/exports/deletes with a re-read check, a safety copy, an in-place rewrite and a read-back compare, converts single saves between .mcs/.psv/.psx/raw and creates new cards in several containers; the format work lives in mc_ps1_card.c and mc_save_export.c.

findings.title: dashLaunchApp rewrites DASHAPPS.CNF before every launch even when the Recent list did not change (or Recent is off)
findings.problem: dashLaunchApp calls dashStorePushRecent unconditionally, and dashStorePushRecent marks the lists dirty even when the path is already recent[0]. settleBackgroundWork (dashStoreFlushWait) then writes the whole DASHAPPS.CNF and reads it back (dashWriteFile, dash_store.c:148-175) and the launch waits for it. Relaunching the top app, the common case, costs a store-dir (often memory card) write each time. It also records Recent when dashCfg.recent_count is 0 (Recent off), which dashLaunchHook (:263) honours.
findings.fix: In dashStorePushRecent return before dashStoreSaveLists when idx is 0 (already first). In dashLaunchApp call dashStorePushRecent only when dashCfg.recent_count > 0, as dashLaunchHook does.
findings.justification: Adds one early return and one condition. Without them every relaunch of the most recent app waits on a full DASHAPPS.CNF write plus read-back on the store device (mc0:/SYS-CONF or beside the ELF). Two conditions are the smallest way to skip that write.
findings.benefit: One DASHAPPS.CNF write + verify read and the launch wait for it saved per launch of the top Recent app or with Recent set to 0 (INFERRED from the call path; time not measured).
findings.evidence: Read dash_main.c:592-682 (push at :649, settleBackgroundWork :652 -> dashStoreFlushWait dash_store.c:670-681 -> dashStoreFlush(1) -> submitSave(SAVE_LISTS) :622-657 -> saveRun -> dashWriteFile :148-175, which always truncates, writes and reads back). dashStorePushRecent :843-861: idx==0 leaves the list unchanged but still calls dashStoreSaveLists (:716-720 sets save_dirty). recent_count 0 means Recent off: dash_settings.c:968 options {0,4,8,12,16}, dash_home.c:104-111 shows only recent_count entries; grep dashLists.recent: no other reader.

findings.title: runLaunchKey writes the launch-key title into the shared library entry
findings.problem: dashLibResolve returns &dashApps[i] when the ELF is in the library, and runLaunchKey then copies setting->LK_Title over a->title. After a boot or SELECT+button launch through a titled key, the library entry keeps the key's title (shown on Home/Applications, out of title sort order) if the launch fails. If dashLaunchApp saves the cache (dash_main.c:647-648, art dirty), dashLibBuildCache writes that title to DASHLIB.CNF and it survives reboots until a rescan.
findings.fix: Apply the title to a copy: when dashLibResolve returned a library entry, memcpy it into tmp first and set tmp.title, then launch &tmp (dashLaunchApp already works on its own copy).
findings.justification: Adds one memcpy. It is the smallest change that keeps a per-key label from overwriting the library title in RAM and in DASHLIB.CNF.
findings.benefit: Library titles and DASHLIB.CNF no longer pick up launch-key labels (minor persistent display bug fixed).
findings.evidence: Read dash_main.c:959-972 (runLaunchKey), :1072-1128 (callers from boot), :979-1019 (quick launch caller). dash_lib.c:454-482: dashLibFind returns &dashApps[i], dashLibResolve returns it before using transient. dash_lib.c:604-640: dashLibSaveCache marks SAVE_CACHE dirty; dashLibBuildCache writes a->title; dashLibLoadCache :583-601 reads it back and sorts by title (titleCmp :484-490). dashLaunchApp :601 copies the app, so launching from a copy changes nothing else.

findings.title: First-run welcome dialog opens during the auto-launch countdown, which then cannot be cancelled
findings.problem: The intro check uses boot_phase != 1, so it fires while boot_phase is 2 (auto-launch countdown). dashModalMessage blocks and takes all input, so 'Press any button to stay' (bootUpdate needs in->any) cannot cancel, while bootDraw keeps showing the countdown underneath. If the user reads past the deadline, the auto key launches on the next frame after the dialog closes. Trigger: from_boot with LK_Path[SETTING_LK_AUTO] set and intro_done 0, i.e. first boot with an existing auto-launch config, or after 'show welcome again' (dash_settings.c:3295-3298).
findings.fix: Show the welcome only when boot_phase is 0 (change the condition to !boot_phase), so it appears after the countdown is cancelled, or not at all when the auto launch happens.
findings.benefit: Auto-launch countdown stays cancellable on the first boot (minor bug fixed, no size change).
findings.evidence: boot_phase is file-static; every use read in dash_main.c (:39, :741, :772, :868, :1072-1153, :1411-1426, :1486, :1517, :1527), none in modal code. bootBegin :1084-1087 sets phase 2 when Init_Delay is 0 and LK auto is set; :1114-1117 after the delay. bootUpdate :1119-1126 cancels only on in->any from the main loop. dashRenderScene :1216 calls bootDraw, so the countdown is drawn under modals. intro_done defaults to 0 (dash_store.c:248). Whether the closing button press is flushed was not traced, hence Med.

findings.title: dashPngDecode leaks the interlaced full-image buffer and row table when libpng fails mid-image
findings.problem: For interlaced images the decoder mallocs full (w*h*4, up to 256*256*4 = 256 KB) and rows (h pointers) as plain locals. A corrupt or truncated interlaced PNG makes png_read_image call png_error, pngErr longjmps to the handler at :77-84, which frees only row, acc, acc_n and dst. full and rows are lost. Covers, theme images and files opened in the image viewer come from user devices, and each failed open leaks again.
findings.fix: Declare full and rows with the other volatile pointers at the top of the function and free them in the setjmp handler, setting them to NULL after their normal frees.
findings.justification: Adds two frees and two declarations. Without them each corrupt interlaced PNG leaks up to 257 KB of EE heap per decode attempt (image viewer re-opens, slideshow over a folder). Freeing in the existing handler is the smallest fix.
findings.benefit: Up to 256 KB + 8 KB (rows) of EE heap no longer leaked per failed interlaced decode (INFERRED: w*h <= 65536 enforced at :96, 4 bytes per pixel; h <= 2048 pointers).
findings.evidence: Read dash_png.c:43-224. pngErr :43-47 longjmps; png_read_image :153 runs after full/rows are allocated at :141/:146 and before free(rows) :154 / free(full) :178. Handler :77-84 frees only row/acc/acc_n/dst. Callers: dash_art.c:343 (artRun worker job), dash_art.c:513 (themeTexRun worker job), dash_image.c:111 (image viewer, UI thread); grep dashPngLoadFile/dashPngDecode over src include: no other callers.

findings.title: dashPngDecode does a 64-bit division per source pixel to map columns and rows
findings.problem: dx = (u64)x * dw / w is computed for every source pixel (and dy per row). The R5900 has no 64-bit divide, so each one is a __udivdi3 call (the builtin is linked into the ELF). A 2048x2048 PNG means about 4.2 million calls. That time lands on the worker (art, theme) or on the UI thread behind the loading overlay (image viewer, dash_image.c:111). The operands never need 64 bits: x, y < 2048 and dw <= w, dh <= h <= 2048, so the products stay below 2^22.
findings.fix: Use 32-bit unsigned arithmetic for dx and dy (drop the u64 casts). Optionally hoist dx into a per-column table computed once per image.
findings.benefit: Removes one 64-bit division call per source pixel: about 4.2M calls for a 2048x2048 image, 1M for 1024x1024 (INFERRED; per-call cycle cost not measured).
findings.evidence: Read dash_png.c:93-203: w,h <= DASH_PNG_MAX_DIM 2048 (:16, :93); dw/dh only shrink (:115-128). evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-archive-members.tsv:181 shows __udivdi3 from libclang_rt.builtins-mips64el.a linked into wLaunchELF (first requester main_title.o). That dash_png.o calls it for these lines is INFERRED from the u64 operands and the R5900 lacking DDIVU; no disassembly was available. Callers and threads: dash_art.c:343/513 (worker jobs), dash_image.c:111 (UI thread with dashLoadingBegin).

findings.title: dash_ps1_card.c keeps 8 KB of tool-only state in .bss for the whole run
findings.problem: p1_saves, p1_titles, p1_details, p1_items and p1_head are static arrays used only while the PS1 card tool is open. The three card buffers are already allocated in p1Hold and freed in p1Drop, but these 8 KB stay resident from boot to exit.
findings.fix: Allocate these arrays in the same p1Hold memalign block as the card buffers (one larger allocation) and drop them with it in p1Drop.
findings.benefit: 8092 B of .bss returned to the heap while the tool is closed (MEASURED: evidence/Launchstation/raw/link/wLaunchELF-contrib-by-object.tsv:74, dash_ps1_card.o .bss 8092).
findings.evidence: Read dash_ps1_card.c:29-36 and every use: p1_saves/p1_titles/p1_details/p1_items only in p1CardTool :592-653; p1_head in p1Load call :600, p1Safety :150, p1Commit :176, p1CopyAs :588. All run between p1Hold :719-731 and p1Drop :733-737 (dashPs1CardTool :739-748, dashPs1CardNew :750-759). Sizes: PS1_CARD_HEAD_MAX 3904 (mc_save_export.h:52), 15*96 + 15*64 + 17*16 (DashMenuItem dash_internal.h:902-908) + 15*sizeof(Ps1CardSave) (mc_ps1_card.h:66-74), totalling the measured 8092.
